name: Tunisian Couscous
description: Couscous, tiny steamed semolina granules topped with a vegetable and meat stew, is Tunisia's most iconic dish, genuinely distinct from its Algerian and Moroccan neighbors through a more assertively spicy, harissa-forward broth.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram), mature seeds, canned, drained solids

ingredients.ingredient: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram), mature seeds, canned, drained solids

steps_detailed: Simmer the chicken, carrot, chickpeas, and harissa seasoning in 1.5 cups water 25-28 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Pour the boiling broth over the dry couscous, cover, and let steam 5 minutes, then fluff.
Serve the stew and broth over the couscous.

name: Tunisian Brik
description: Brik, a thin pastry fried until crisp and traditionally enclosing a whole runny egg, is one of Tunisia's most iconic dishes - the yolk staying soft inside the crackling-crisp shell is the entire point, not a mistake to fix.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Fish, tuna, light, canned in water, drained solids

ingredients.ingredient: Fish, tuna, light, canned in water, drained solids

steps_detailed: Layer the tuna in the center of a phyllo sheet, crack the egg on top, and fold into a triangle, sealing the edges carefully so the yolk stays intact.
Fry immediately, 1-2 minutes per side, just until the pastry is golden and crisp - the yolk should still be soft and runny inside.

name: Tunisian Makroudh
description: Makroudh, semolina pastries filled with dates and soaked in honey, a beloved Tunisian sweet shared with the wider Maghreb.
steps_detailed: Mix the semolina and melted butter with a little water into a firm dough.
Flatten, place the chopped dates in the center, and fold to seal.
Bake at 350F (175C) for 20-22 minutes until golden.
Soak in warm honey while still warm.
